 Principal Seat At Jabalpur

sentences.text: Shri Amit Dubey, counsel for the respondent.
1. This miscellaneous criminal case has been instituted on an application under Section 378 (3) of the Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the State for leave appeal against judgment of acquittal.

It is directed against the judgment dated 10.01.2013 passed by the Court of JMFC, Hoshangabad, in Criminal Case No.79/2011 acquitting accused/respondent Hari Shankar Agrawal of the charge under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to in this order as the Act).

2. The facts necessary for disposal of this application for leave to appeal under Section 378(3) of the Cr.P.C. are that a complaint for offence under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(1) of the Act was filed on behalf of the Dy. Director of Food and Drug Administration, Hoshangabad, against the accused/respondent Hari Shankar Agrawal for selling Adulterated besan laddus.

After trial,
learned Magistrate recorded a finding that complainant Food Inspector Jagdish Prasad Lavwanshi was authorized to take sample of aforesaid food article from the accused/respondent.
On the date of the offence, besan laddus were sold by the accused to the complainant.

The sample so taken was found to be adulterated and the complaint was properly filed; however, relying upon the judgment rendered by a co- ordinate bench of this Court in the case of Banshi Lal Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2003 (4) MPLJ 169. accused/respondent was acquitted of the charge solely on the ground that the notice under Section 13 (2) of the Act was served upon one Vimla Agrawal and no evidence had been led to prove in what manner , if at all, aforesaid Vimla Agrawal is related to the accused.

entities.text: Banshi Lal Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2003 (4) MPLJ 169
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, mandatory provision of section 13 (2) of the Act was not complied with.

sentences.text:
In view of various authorities like Ajit Prasad Vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1972 Supreme Court 1631, Babulal Hargovind Das Vs. State of Gujrat, AIR 1971 Supreme Court 1277 and Govind Prasad Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 1996 Cr.L.J 1238 etc., the leave to appeal against acquittal deserves to be granted, so that the question may be reconsidered.
4.

This miscellaneous criminal case stands disposed of.

5. Let criminal appeal against acquittal be registered.
6. Let a warrant bailable in the sum of Rs.20,000/- be issued against the respondent/accused Hari Shankar Agrawal for securing his presence before this Court on 21.6.2016 and thereafter before the Registry on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard.
